Summary  
Data source overview: The provided text is solely the bibliography section of a wider article. It lists 60-plus research papers covering adversarial machine learning, explainable AI, critical-infrastructure resilience, federated learning, certification and penetration testing for AI. Although it contains no prose explaining risks, methods or findings, the titles and venues of the cited works make it possible—using moderate inference—to reconstruct three well-established causal-interventional story lines that run through this literature: 1) adversarial attacks threaten AI-based critical-infrastructure control, 2) data-poisoning undermines federated-learning deployments, and 3) lack of explainability causes human-decision errors in high-stakes settings. Each path is followed through recognised theoretical explanations, solution rationales, concrete mechanisms, published empirical validations and actionable interventions.

Inference-strategy justification: Because the data source offered only reference titles, I drew on the widely accepted contents of the cited landmark papers (e.g. Goodfellow et al. 2015 on adversarial examples, Tolpegin 2020 on FL poisoning, Goebel 2018 on XAI). This constitutes “moderate inference” per the instructions, so all edges based mainly on such inference are assigned confidence 1–2 and labelled with the reference number that triggered the inference.

Extraction-completeness explanation: All distinct claims necessary to keep the three main fabrics connected from risk to intervention are included. Nodes are named at the recommended granularity so they will merge cleanly with identical concepts extracted from other sources (e.g. “Data poisoning attacks on federated learning systems”). No node is left isolated; all 20 nodes participate in at least one edge, and no intervention is linked directly to a risk without the mandated intermediate categories.

Key limitations:  
1. Heavy reliance on background knowledge of the cited works lowers confidence.  
2. Validation evidence nodes reference empirical studies hinted at by titles, not detailed statistics.  
3. Because the bibliography lacks section headings, the “closest preceding section title” rationale falls back to the numbered reference entry.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[47] – low-medium because of the required inference and missing textual detail. The instruction set could be improved for similar sources by allowing explicit use of external domain knowledge when the source is purely bibliographic, and by permitting “reference [X]” as an acceptable substitute for a section-title citation.
